grammar.title: Causative: Have/Get Something Done
grammar.explanation:
Sometimes another person does the work for you. You arrange it and you pay for it, but you do not do it yourself.

English has a special causative structure for exactly this situation, from phone repairs to podcast editing. The core pattern is **have + object + past participle**.

This pattern tells the listener that someone else performed the action as a service for you. The focus is on the result you received.

You can also use **get + object + past participle**. This version is more informal, and it is very common in everyday conversation.

Word order matters. The object always comes before the **past participle**, and the participle itself never changes form.

This structure is different from the present perfect. **Have something done** focuses on the service you received, not on an action you performed yourself, like fixing your own firewall.
examples: I *had my laptop repaired* yesterday. (a technician fixed it for me)
She *got her hair cut* before the webinar. (informal; at a salon)
We *had our firewall installed* by an expert. (a security service)
He *got his podcast edited* by a professional. (someone else did the editing)
They *had all the computers rebooted* after the attack. (the IT team did it)
The influencer *had her video filmed* by a small team. (she did not film it herself)

practice.q: Rewrite with the causative: A technician repaired my phone.
Rewrite with the causative: Someone cleans our office every evening.
practice.a: We have our office cleaned every evening.

practice.q: Rewrite with get (informal): An expert checked my firewall.
Rewrite with the causative: A designer will build our website.
practice.a: We will have our website built by a designer.

practice.q: Rewrite with the causative: The mechanic is servicing her car now.
practice.a: She is having her car serviced.

practice.q: Rewrite with get: They delivered our new microphone yesterday.
practice.a: We got our new microphone delivered yesterday.

practice.q: True or false: 'I have cut my hair' and 'I have had my hair cut' mean the same thing.
practice.a: False. In the first, you cut it yourself; in the second, someone else cut it.

practice.q: Fix the word order: 'I had repaired my laptop by a technician.'
practice.a: I had my laptop repaired by a technician.

practice.q: Rewrite with the causative: Someone took a screenshot of the error for me.
practice.a: I had a screenshot taken of the error message.

practice.q: Make a causative sentence: you / your spam filter / update (last week).
practice.a: I had my spam filter updated last week.
